_about: The pictures chosen for the buttons' signs and the top bar (standin_icons_make.py). n: the picture's number on its sheet (from: another sign's sheet); title: a Commons file by name; cut: left, top, right, bottom as shares of the picture; mode: dark (a thing on a plain ground) or lines (a drawing); kind toned: it keeps its light and shade.

coin.says: A silver denier of Charlemagne struck at Dorestad before the new coinage of 793/4: the side that names the town, DOR STAT, over an axe.

cast_off.says: A ship of the north under sail, drawn for 'Social Scandinavia in the Viking Age' (1920).

voyage.says: The gilded vane of a ship's prow, which shows the wind (Soderala, Sweden, about 1000; Swedish History Museum).

crew.says: A fighting man in a wolf's skin, from one of the bronze plates of Torslunda (Oland, about 600), as drawn.

hold.says: The oak chest of Mastermyr (Gotland, Viking Age; Swedish History Museum).

trade.says: A merchant's folding balance (Swedish History Museum).

alehouse.says: A jug of Tating ware, the fine Rhineland pitcher of about 800 (Swedish History Museum).

offer.says: The pectoral cross of St Cuthbert (Northumbria, 7th century), as a drawing.

rest.says: A fire steel, struck on flint to light the fire (Swedish History Museum).

look_out.says: The helmet of Sutton Hoo (East Anglia, about 625), its eyes on you.

sound.says: The lead and its line, from Paasch's Illustrated Marine Encyclopedia (1890).

hail.says: A horn of ivory, the 'horn of Roland' (11th century, Musee Paul Dupuy, Toulouse).

wares.says: A round-bottomed pot of Frisian make, found in a grave at Birka (Swedish History Museum).

journey.says: A wax tablet and its stylus (a replica).

errands.says: Tally sticks, notched and split (medieval, Winchester City Museums).

book.says: The cover of the St Cuthbert Gospel (Northumbria, early 8th century).
